description: Our team has skills in software development,AI/ML, data analysis, and UI/UX design We can build interactive web applications and dashboards,work with datasets, detect patterns and anomalies,and create clear visualizations For this challenge, we aim to develop an intelligent astronaut health monitoring system that analyzes health data,detects potential anomalies,and provides clear risk alerts
summary: SpaceHealth is a health monitoring platform that supports astronauts during space missions. A smartwatch-style wearable collects continuous physiological indicators, which are transferred to the application through APIs, organized, analyzed, and displayed on an interactive health dashboard. Unlike conventional health-monitoring apps that rely on Earth-based standards, SpaceHealth uses an adaptive approach designed for space. It tracks each astronaut’s individual baseline, accounts for microgravity-related physiological changes, and flags unusual deviations. The current prototype uses simulated data, and wearable integration is the next planned step.
details:
How it works:

Each daily record (heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, sleep, stress, mood, radiation dose, and cabin CO₂ and oxygen) is compared with the astronaut’s own recent history of 7 to 14 records. A z-score measures how far each value departs from that baseline. An Isolation Forest, a standard machine-learning method, checks whether the overall combination of readings is unusual, and trend rules detect multi-day changes. A transparent rule engine then assigns one of three levels.

Normal, Attention Required, or High Priority Alert. High Priority requires several signals, including at least one major signal or two trends, so a single minor spike cannot trigger it.

Modules:

Physical monitoring shows vitals and cabin conditions with short trends:

Radiation monitoring is the top priority: it shows dose in mSv/day, marks statistical deviations as not validated exposure limits, and shows NOAA space-weather data only as timestamped context. Well-being includes a daily voice log stored on the device, reminders, and a Space Companion that suggests calming, non-diagnostic routines and family-message ideas. A 3D anatomy view shows simulated muscle and bone status.

Benefits:

Faster awareness of changes, fewer false alarms through personal baselines, autonomy under communication delay, and clear guidance for crew without technical training.

Tools:

React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js for the interface; Python, FastAPI, NumPy, scikit-learn, and SQLite for analysis and storage; Node.js and Express for the family message server; pytest and Playwright for testing; Replit for development and hosting.

Limits:

The system uses synthetic data, has no real sensors, no user authentication in the API prototype, and no clinical validation.
